chunks: 5392 - And Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from Abū al-Jārūd, who said:
I heard Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: “The mule of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was not turned back from anything it entered.”

He said: “Then a man from Banū Mudlij came while it had entered a reed field belonging to him, so he fitted an arrow for it and killed it.” Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said to him: “By Allah, you shall not leave me until you pay compensation for it.” He said: “So he compensated for it with six hundred dirhams.”

key_terms.بَغْلَةُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the mule belonging to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.بَنِي مُدْلِجٍ: the tribe of Mudlij mentioned in the report
key_terms.تَدِيَهَا: to pay its compensation or indemnity
key_terms.سَهْمًا: an arrow used to kill the animal
key_terms.سِتَّمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ: six hundred dirhams, the amount of compensation
key_terms.قَصَبٍ: a reed field or area of reeds

ai.seo_question: What compensation was paid for killing the mule of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts that a man killed the mule of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله after it entered his reed field. Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام required him to provide compensation, and the value paid was six hundred dirhams. The report is relevant to discussions of liability, compensation, and financial responsibility for destroyed property.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5392 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Abu Al-Jarud who said:

I heard Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) say:
"The mule of the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) was never stopped from going anywhere it wanted."

Imam (as) said: "A man from Banu Mudlij came, and the mule had entered his field of reeds. He prepared an arrow and killed it."
Then Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said to him: "By Allah (swt), you will not leave me until you compensate for it."
So he compensated for it with six hundred dirhams.
